claims.paraphrased_claim: DNR: in spring, walleye are commonly concentrated in near-shore locations, especially big sand flats, feeding on schools of shiner minnows.
Jig-and-minnow is standard technique for presenting bait to shallow-feeding walleye; DNR describes the seasonal location, not this exact rig.
Light spinning tackle is standard for casting small jigs to shallow structure.
Standard shallow-water jig weight range for this presentation.
Standard hop-and-pause cadence for jig-and-minnow.
Follows from the DNR-documented seasonal shift to deeper mid-lake structure as the season progresses.

retrieve.depth_control: count down to bottom, hop along it

tactics.rigging_instructions: Plain jig tipped with a shiner minnow, cast to shallow sand flats and worked back with short hops.
tactics.bite_detection: A tap or the line coming tight as the fish moves off.
tactics.hookset_fight: Firm sweep-set once weight is felt.
tactics.works_when: Early spring, water still cold, walleye concentrated on shallow sand flats feeding on shiner schools.
tactics.fails_when: Once water warms past the spring window and fish disperse to deeper structure -- see the summer slip-sinker tactic instead.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No fish located after working several flats -- fish may have already moved, try deeper adjacent structure.

retrieve.rod_position: tip low, feed slack on the take

tactics.rigging_instructions: Slip sinker above a swivel, fluorocarbon leader to a hook baited with minnow, nightcrawler, or leech, dragged near bottom on humps/flats.
tactics.bite_detection: Light taps or steady building pressure.
tactics.hookset_fight: Feed slack, then sweep-set into steady pressure.
tactics.works_when: Mid-summer, warm stable water, fish holding on deep mid-lake structure.
tactics.fails_when: Cold water or real current -- too subtle/slow to hold position or register a bite.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No contact after working 3-4 distinct structure spots thoroughly.
tactics.conservation_notes: Fish from 20ft+ may show barotrauma signs; consider a descending device for release.

retrieve.depth_control: small perch-pattern crank run near bottom over the target depth

tactics.rigging_instructions: Small hard-bodied crankbait resembling perch, cast or trolled along shoreline structure.
tactics.bite_detection: A hard strike, rod loads immediately.
tactics.hookset_fight: Let the fish load a moderate-action rod; no manual hookset usually needed.
tactics.works_when: Early-mid fall as walleye return to shoreline structure; low light/chop improves it.
tactics.fails_when: Bright, calm, clear conditions in the same season make the same shallow presentation too visible.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: Follows or short strikes without hookup -- slow down or downsize before abandoning the pattern.

alternatives.note: Genuinely different seasonal pattern (fall shallow vs. summer deep); not a same-conditions disagreement.

retrieve.cadence: sharp upward snaps with a flutter on the fall, occasionally slapping bottom to create a sediment plume
retrieve.depth_control: work within a few feet of bottom
retrieve.rod_position: active, high hand position between snaps

tactics.rigging_instructions: Flashy fluttering jigging spoon, worked aggressively near bottom; can be fished bare or tipped with a waxworm/minnow head.
tactics.bite_detection: A sudden stop on the fall or a hard thump on the upstroke.
tactics.hookset_fight: Sharp upward set on any unnatural weight or stop.
tactics.works_when: Midwinter, clear water, over deep structure, when fish are actively responding to flash/vibration and reaction strikes.
tactics.fails_when: When fish are neutral/inactive and spook from or ignore aggressive movement -- see the deadstick alternative.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: Fish marked on electronics but not committing to the aggressive presentation -- switch to the subtler deadstick tactic rather than continuing to work it harder.

alternatives.note: DNR's own ice-fishing-walleye page explicitly frames aggressive jigging-spoon action and a near-motionless minnow-head jig as competing approaches under the SAME conditions (same water, same depth, same time of year) without declaring either universally correct -- a genuine, sourced disagreement, not a condition-window difference. Confidence on both sides is anecdotal/practitioner-level, not established.

retrieve.depth_control: held just above bottom or at the marked fish depth

tactics.rigging_instructions: Small jig in a minnow shape/color tipped with a minnow head, held nearly still at the fish's depth.
tactics.bite_detection: Very subtle -- a slight line twitch or the bobber/spring bobber loading almost imperceptibly.
tactics.hookset_fight: A gentle, deliberate lift rather than a hard snap -- an aggressive set can pull the bait from a light-biting fish.
tactics.works_when: Midwinter, clear water, when fish are neutral/inactive or have been pressured and shy away from aggressive movement.
tactics.fails_when: When fish are actively feeding and a subtler presentation gets outcompeted or simply not noticed -- see the aggressive spoon alternative.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: Fish approach on electronics but do not commit -- if this ALSO fails to draw a take within a reasonable window, try the aggressive spoon instead (and vice versa); the DNR itself does not resolve which comes first.

alternatives.note: Same genuine disagreement, other direction -- see t4's note.

retrieve.cadence: lift-drop, maintain bottom contact between lifts
retrieve.depth_control: count down to bottom, lift just clear then settle

tactics.rigging_instructions: Jig tied direct, tipped with a minnow, cast upstream/across current seams and worked back with bottom-contact hops.
tactics.bite_detection: A tap, sudden slack, extra weight, or the line moving differently from the current.
tactics.hookset_fight: Sweep-set on any contact -- current fish often only tap once.
tactics.works_when: Pre-spawn river/tributary staging, moderate current, walleye and sauger holding on seams and channel edges.
tactics.fails_when: Once fish move onto true spawning gravel (different, more localized behavior) or in dead-still water with no seam to define.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No contact after working 3-4 current seams at the right depth/pace -- try a heavier jig to hold bottom better, or relocate to the next seam downstream.

retrieve.depth_control: set the slip bobber stop to hold bait at the drop-off depth
retrieve.rod_position: resting or hand-held near the dock

tactics.rigging_instructions: Slip bobber set to depth, small hook with a minnow or leech, suspended near a dock drop-off.
tactics.bite_detection: The bobber goes under or moves off at an angle.
tactics.hookset_fight: Wait for the bobber to fully submerge before a firm sweep-set.
tactics.works_when: Low light (dawn/dusk), docks adjacent to a drop-off, early summer.
tactics.fails_when: Bright midday light with fish holding deeper off the drop-off, out of easy dock-casting range.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No action at dawn/dusk after a reasonable wait -- try adjusting depth before abandoning the spot.

retrieve.depth_control: count down to just above bottom

tactics.rigging_instructions: Small light jig (bare or minnow-tipped) fished quietly from a kayak/canoe over a clear-water point, fluorocarbon leader to reduce visibility.
tactics.bite_detection: A subtle tick or the line twitching sideways.
tactics.hookset_fight: Light, deliberate sweep-set -- light line requires smooth drag use.
tactics.works_when: Clear water, calm conditions, where a quiet low-profile platform and finesse presentation out-fish a noisier boat approach.
tactics.fails_when: Windy/chop conditions where a kayak/canoe becomes difficult to control and hold position on structure.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: Difficulty holding position in wind is itself the signal to switch platforms/tactics, not a bait problem.

retrieve.depth_control: bottom-bouncer or leadcore to hold near bottom

tactics.rigging_instructions: Spinner-blade crawler harness trolled behind a bottom-bouncer, high-contrast blade color for turbid water.
tactics.bite_detection: Steady rod-tip load; strikes are usually decisive on a moving bait.
tactics.hookset_fight: Let the moving bait set the hook; trim speed only after a confirmed hookup pattern emerges.
tactics.works_when: Turbid/stained water where flash and vibration matter more than visual color match, covering water to relocate scattered fish.
tactics.fails_when: Clear water where a more natural, subtler presentation typically outperforms a flashy trolled harness.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No takers after a full pass -- change blade color/size or speed before changing location.

retrieve.cadence: hold in current with just enough weight to maintain bottom contact
retrieve.depth_control: walk the rig downstream through the hole

tactics.rigging_instructions: Heavier slip-sinker rig to hold bottom in current, fluorocarbon leader, minnow or shiner in a deep river channel hole.
tactics.bite_detection: A distinct tap-tap-tap or a steady heavy pull, distinct from the drag of current.
tactics.hookset_fight: Firm sweep-set once weight is confirmed as a fish, not current drag.
tactics.works_when: Fall river/tailwater staging, sauger holding in deep, turbid channel holes -- sauger tolerate current and turbidity more readily than walleye in the same reach.
tactics.fails_when: Clear, still conditions where sauger are typically found shallower or more dispersed, not stacked in deep turbid holes.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: Consistent snags/no bites in one hole after real effort -- move to the next channel bend rather than adding more weight.

alternatives.note: Same presentation family (slip-sinker) adapted for current/turbidity and sauger rather than stillwater walleye -- a real species/environment variant, not a duplicate.

retrieve.depth_control: shallow-running crank, count down briefly then reel

tactics.rigging_instructions: Small shallow-running crankbait fan-cast from shore/wading along a stained-water point, no bait needed.
tactics.bite_detection: A solid thump, rod loads on its own.
tactics.hookset_fight: Let the moving lure set the hook.
tactics.works_when: Post-spawn, low light, shore-accessible points in stained water where an artificial-only, bait-free approach is fully viable.
tactics.fails_when: Bright midday light or very clear water where a shallow crank is too visible for a wary post-spawn fish.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No follows/strikes after several fan-cast passes -- try a slower retrieve before changing lures.

retrieve.depth_control: held just off bottom near a river-mouth basin

tactics.rigging_instructions: Small minnow-head jig fished nearly still near a river-mouth basin under early ice.
tactics.bite_detection: A very subtle tap, easy to miss.
tactics.works_when: Early ice, sauger holding in stained basin areas near a river/tributary inlet.
tactics.fails_when: Once fish scatter to open-basin suspension later in winter -- reassess location, not just presentation.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No marks on electronics near the river mouth -- try progressively further into the basin.

alternatives.note: Same presentation family as the walleye deadstick tactic, adapted to sauger and an early-ice river-mouth location.

retrieve.depth_control: set shallower than the clear-water version -- stained water needs less depth to stay hidden

tactics.rigging_instructions: Same slip-bobber livebait rig as the clear-water dock tactic, set shallower since stained water already reduces visibility to fish.
tactics.hookset_fight: Wait for full submersion, then a firm sweep-set.
tactics.works_when: Stained water reduces the low-light requirement of the clear-water version -- viable across more of the day.
tactics.fails_when: Turbid water where visual bobber-fishing gives way to a bait presentation that does not depend on fish sighting it.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: No action across several hours at varying depths -- the dock itself may simply not have fish nearby today.

alternatives.note: Same platform/presentation family as the clear-water dock tactic, varied by clarity condition -- not a duplicate, a real condition-driven variant.

retrieve.cadence: heavy enough weight to hold in strong current, otherwise still
retrieve.depth_control: anchor position on the slower inside edge of the current seam
retrieve.rod_position: braced rod holder, strong current load

tactics.rigging_instructions: Heavier slip-sinker rig scaled up for strong post-rain current, fished on the slower inside edge of a channel seam.
tactics.bite_detection: Distinct pull against the already-loaded rod tip, distinct from current surge.
tactics.hookset_fight: Firm set given the heavier terminal tackle; expect a harder-pulling fight in current.
tactics.works_when: Rising, turbid water after heavy rain, fish pushed to current-breaks on channel edges rather than the main flow.
tactics.fails_when: Once the river stabilizes/clears, this scaled-up heavy rig becomes unnecessarily coarse -- downsize toward tactic 6 or 10 instead.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: Constant snagging/no bites in the main current -- the fish are very unlikely to be fighting the strongest flow; move to a slower inside seam.

alternatives.note: Same species pairing and river environment as t6, scaled up specifically for high-water/heavy-current conditions rather than normal pre-spawn flow.
Related sauger river tactic at normal flow; this is the elevated-water variant.

retrieve.cadence: as close to no movement as possible
retrieve.depth_control: held precisely at the fish-marked depth
retrieve.rod_position: resting, watch the line/spring bobber only

tactics.rigging_instructions: The smallest practical live-bait presentation, fished essentially motionless -- late-ice, post-front, suspected low-oxygen conditions call for minimizing everything that could spook an already-stressed, sluggish fish.
tactics.bite_detection: Extremely subtle -- watch for the faintest line movement, do not rely on feel.
tactics.hookset_fight: A very gentle, deliberate lift -- an aggressive set is likely to miss or pull free from a barely-committed bite.
tactics.works_when: Late ice, immediately after a front has passed, in a deep basin area where low dissolved oxygen is a documented seasonal risk (long ice cover + snow load) -- fish are sluggish and easily put off by movement or noise.
tactics.fails_when: Once oxygen conditions genuinely recover (typically post-turnover after ice-out) or on a stable-weather day where fish are actively feeding -- this presentation is unnecessarily passive for active fish.
tactics.diagnostic_signals: Marks on electronics that will not commit even to this presentation may indicate the DO-stress read is correct and the bite window is simply very short -- minimize noise/hole-hopping rather than changing presentation further.
tactics.conservation_notes: Fish in a genuinely low-oxygen late-ice scenario are under real physiological stress; minimize air exposure and handling time on any catch.

alternatives.note: Same deadstick presentation family as t5, taken further (even less movement, smaller profile) for the specific late-ice/post-front/low-DO-suspected combination.

provisions.official_wording: Statewide inland default: 6 walleye+sauger combined, only one over 20 inches.
Statewide inland default: only one walleye over 20 inches in possession.
Anglers will be able to harvest walleye 17 inches or greater in length, with only one over 20 inches allowed in possession.
Minimum 17 inches to harvest on Mille Lacs Lake.
Catch-and-release walleye/sauger fishing is permitted year-round statewide subject to normal handling requirements.
